memory_candidates.content: When extracting a shared library out of a mutual duplicate-block pair, use the sliding-window detector's own unit of measure (script-inventory.sh's 10-line normalized window) to scope the extraction precisely to what it flags -- in a CLI-tool pair this is typically just the color palette, the option-parsing loop, and the path/file-collection loop, never the tool-specific check logic. Verify behavioral equivalence by diffing the pre/post-refactor output byte-for-byte over a constructed fixture that exercises every finding class, plus every CLI edge case (no args, --help, a bad path, an unknown option) -- these edge-case code paths are exactly what the extracted CLI-parsing block controls and are easy to omit from a 'does it still find the same bugs' check that focuses only on the main-path findings.

git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check drops any files_touched path not matching the task's declared file_scope, even when the edit (e.g. a manifest.json registration for a newly extracted lib file) is a legitimate, necessary incidental touch. This is drop-and-warn by design, not a bug to work around: recover the dropped path with a small, explicitly-labeled follow-up commit via git-commit-scoped.sh directly (never widen the phase commit's pathspec or add the path to file_scope reflexively). The commit message should name which path was dropped and why it was legitimate.
